summary: This turn settled the open AddVoter question from source, using the library's own tests as a third witness. The public doc comment says a server added by AddVoter becomes a staging member that the leader promotes once it is ready, and the membership notes list catch-up before granting a vote as a goal; but nextConfiguration writes Suffrage Voter into the very entry that adds the member, Staging is only left by the Promote case, no non-test caller issues Promote, and configuration.go's own command table says AddStaging was in fact AddVoter and deprecates it in its favour. The in-tree unit expectations resolve which side is intended: the AddVoter cases expect a Voter for a member that was missing, Staging or Nonvoter, mirroring the AddStaging cases exactly, so the implementation matches its tested intent and the public documentation is what misleads. I recorded this as one source-decided interpretation with the conclusion explained (source-only answers cannot claim a measured result) and a defect claim scoped to the documented contract, and I kept the counterweights that argue for reading the prose as stale rather than violated, including that consensus safety is unaffected because log comparison still stops a less up-to-date candidate from winning, so the cost is availability planning rather than correctness. The knowledge entry for the immediate-voter behaviour is cited as the relied-on premise by its exact ID and revision. I also queued an end-to-end witness that joins a fresh empty node through the public API, records the suffrage the leader wrote and the suffrage the new node sees, then disconnects one original voter and checks whether a new command still commits - which it can only do if the freshly added member counts as a voter rather than the non-voting member the documentation describes. All three earlier witnessed findings, the configuration index, duties lost at shutdown, and the vote-less transfer with its control and reproduction, remain recorded and are unaffected.
